headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: next-ai-draw-io’s broad egress/MCP/browser stack can expose shared inputs, while godot_rl_agents has no egress and no shared-channel protections.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists because agent_b uses browsers and MCP, so it may ingest untrusted content; agent_a has no shared channel or parser surface documented, so the pairwise risk is inferred rather than directly evidenced. The interaction is not provably blocked, but the bridge is not explicit in either profile.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests browser or MCP content as instructions
IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b without sanitization
mitigations: Disable browser-driven instruction following for agent_b
Require provenance tags on any content passed from agent_a to agent_b
Use a manual review step before agent_b acts on external text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and prompt-separation guards

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles files, images, PDFs, and API keys and has broad network egress, while agent_a has no egress and no data classes touched. There is no documented shared workspace, so leakage is not proven, but if they share inputs or files, agent_b can transmit sensitive content outward.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file set
IF agent_b sends file contents to a third-party API
mitigations: Keep agent_b on a separate workspace from agent_a
Remove or restrict agent_b network egress during shared tasks
Do not place secrets/API keys in files visible to agent_b
Review outbound requests from agent_b before enabling them
requires-engineering: add per-file redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b supports multiple instances and writes to files/diagrams, but agent_a exposes no write or network surfaces. With no overlapping mutable resource documented, direct conflict is limited; uncertainty stays low because the pair lacks a shared write target in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF agent_b instances modify the same diagram file concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes to shared diagram files
Use file locking for any shared workspace
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a document-processing system that can render or act on inputs, and agent_a can produce outputs that may be treated as upstream content. No verification chain is documented, so if agent_b consumes agent_a output directly, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or documents.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input
IF no human or programmatic verification step exists between them
mitigations: Insert a verification step before agent_b consumes agent_a output
Require source citations for any facts passed onward
Limit agent_b to draft-only mode for agent_a-derived content
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles PDFs, text, images, diagrams, and API keys with broad egress, creating a plausible retention/residency mismatch risk if regulated data is introduced. agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not the compliance driver; the concern is agent_b’s documented external transmission surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII or PHI is loaded into agent_b
IF agent_b forwards that data to external model APIs
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through agent_b
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive documents only
Disable external API providers for regulated workflows
Review retention settings before processing sensitive files
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
